links.outcome: Compared generalist GPT-5 against domain-specific models and GPT-4o on mammography tasks
links.effect: Specialized mammography systems exceed 80% accuracy versus GPT-5's 52% to 64%; GPT-5 outperformed GPT-4o by 10% to 40% in mammography tasks.
links.quote: However, performance remained moderate in neuroradiology (44% macro-average accuracy) and lagged substantially behind domain-specific models in mammography, where specialized systems exceed 80% accuracy compared with GPT-5's 52% to 64%.

links.outcome: Gap between general benchmark/exam performance and specialized perception-critical clinical task performance
links.effect: Strong gains on text benchmarks (over 25 points on MedXpertQA) but moderate neuroradiology accuracy (44% macro-average) and 52% to 64% on mammography.
links.quote: However, performance remained moderate in neuroradiology (44% macro-average accuracy) and lagged substantially behind domain-specific models in mammography, where specialized systems exceed 80% accuracy compared with GPT-5's 52% to 64%.

screen.reason: The paper benchmarks the GPT-5 family against predecessor models across multiple medical licensing, QA, and multimodal radiology/pathology datasets, evaluating baseline diagnostic and clinical reasoning performance without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
